quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: To reduce headlight glare at night, where should you look?

options.text: Straight ahead.
Over your shoulder.
At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. The glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the pavement mean?

options.text: Drivers may make the movement shown by the arrow if they choose to.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are not working.
Drivers must always stop before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while following traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the pavement tells drivers in that lane which direction they must go. Always follow traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic lights from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.
Green, yellow, red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic signal, red is always on top and green is always on the bottom. On a horizontal signal, red is always on the left and green is always on the right.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can do so safely.
Do not move your vehicle under any circumstances.
Wait for the police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if it is safe to do so. Always stay at the scene, identify yourself, and help if needed.

questions.question: When is it okay to drive across or park on a median?

options.text: When you need to rest.
When you need to make a phone call.
When you want to turn around.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive across or park on a median. It is not safe.

questions.question: How can you avoid hitting vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Adjust your rearview mirrors every few minutes.
Honk your horn right before turning or changing lanes.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head quickly to check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before turning or changing lanes, turn your head and glance over your shoulder to see if your blind spot is clear. Do not rely on mirrors alone.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow.
White.
Yellow and white.
Yellow, white, and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Less when drinking beer instead of wine.
Less when drinking wine instead of beer.
Most when drinking hard ciders and mixed drinks.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol harms your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream matters.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means you can go, but you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
It means you can go only if a circular green light is also showing.
It points to the nearest airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means you can go, but you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go, but you must turn in the direction shown. Traffic in that lane must follow the arrow.

questions.question: What are signs called that require drivers to obey an instruction?

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do or not do. If you do not follow them, you can be punished.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs prepare drivers for road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the road has curves. Slow down and be ready to turn.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal. Look for other drivers also moving into your lane. Never use your cell phone while driving to check road conditions.

questions.question: A solid red arrow in a traffic signal:

options.text: Is never used as a traffic signal.
Means the same thing as a circular red light.
Means drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Means traffic in that direction must go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means the same thing as a circular red light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow has the same meaning as a circular red light. Traffic must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:

options.text: Flat.
Curvy.
In the sun.
Shaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: In cold weather, shaded areas under trees or buildings freeze first. These areas also take the longest to dry. Drive carefully on shaded road sections.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to spot tailgaters. If a car is too close, slow down gradually and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because of following too closely.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with opposite traffic, you should:

options.text: Return to your lane when you have enough room between you and the passed vehicle.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when you have enough room between you and the passed vehicle.
questions.explanation: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, move back to the right lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and don't need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before crossing railroad tracks, make sure you have enough room to get all the way across without stopping. Never pass other vehicles at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights approaches?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles with sirens or flashing lights. Pull to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: The most effective way to reduce injury or death in a crash is to:

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Drive only on weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on highways.
Drive only between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective thing you can do to prevent death or injury in a crash.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb:

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your wheels slightly right.
Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. This stops your vehicle from rolling into traffic if it moves. On streets with no curb, turn wheels toward the road edge.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
Flagger ahead.
Two-way left turn.
Turn right or go through.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign. It tells drivers that left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Your driver's license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must carry and show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance whenever you drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is coming.

questions.question: This is a ____ sign.

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield
Do not enter

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a Yield sign. Slow down and let other traffic pass. Stop only if needed. Give the right-of-way to pedestrians and other vehicles.

questions.question: When driving on highways, you should:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stay alert and keep your eyes moving to avoid highway hypnosis. Do not stare at one spot for more than a few seconds. Be ready to react to unexpected dangers.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are extra slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
You need more distance to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery because your tires sit on a thin layer of water, oil, and dirt. Slow down to avoid losing grip. Leave extra space to stop. Watch for standing water and hydroplaning.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a green light, but traffic is coming toward you. You should:

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: You can enter the intersection when the light is green to prepare for your left turn. Wait in the center until oncoming traffic passes, then complete your turn.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar car from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry because all cars are the same.
Hide that you do not know the car.
Ignore any obvious problems to not embarrass your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how it works before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where everything is and how it works before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving, find and understand the turn signals, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive. Do not drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more at night.
You cannot see as far in the dark.
It rains more at night.
You see more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Use your headlights. Drive slowly enough so you can stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
Divided highway starts.
Divided highway ends.
Bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: Before starting your car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your seat belt and check that all passengers do the same before you start driving.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your vision?

options.text: You can see more of the road.
You can see less of the road.
It is easier to see cars coming from the side.
Your vision does not change.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see less of the road.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your field of vision gets smaller. This means you need to be more alert to dangers around you.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and check if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and check if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren but cannot see where it is coming from, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until you know the emergency vehicle is not heading toward you.

questions.question: When are roads most slippery from rain?

options.text: After it has been raining for over an hour.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery at the start of rain because the water brings oil from the road surface up to the top. This problem is worse in hot weather because the heat causes even more oil to rise to the surface.

questions.question: When must children wear seat belts?

options.text: Anytime they are in a moving car.
Only if their parents say they should.
Only if they want to.
Only if they weigh less than 100 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anytime they are in a moving car.
questions.explanation: Florida law requires all children under 18 to wear a fastened seat belt whenever they are in a moving car, no matter where they sit.

questions.question: You see a flashing red traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, let other traffic pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: How long does a DUI conviction stay on your driving record?

options.text: One year.
10 years.
40 years.
75 years.

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 years.
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence is very dangerous. The penalties are strict, including heavy fines, higher insurance costs, loss of license, and jail time. A DUI conviction stays on your record for 75 years.

questions.question: What does this speed limit sign mean?

options.text: You must drive at this exact speed.
The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must drive through the intersection at this speed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed allowed on the road. In bad weather like rain, snow, or ice, you should drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: If someone is injured in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless you must. Moving them carelessly can make minor injuries worse. Keep them warm while waiting for help. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol, how can you drive safely?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with someone who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Wait 30 minutes before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with someone who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The safest way to avoid drunk driving is to arrange a ride with a friend who has not been drinking. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your blood. Your body takes about an hour to get rid of the alcohol in one drink.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have big blind spots in front, on the sides, and in the back. Stay out of these areas. Because of their size and weight, trucks need more space to turn and stop than regular cars.

questions.question: A person who drives much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be dangerous. If you are on a two-lane road and cars are backing up behind you, you must pull over and let them pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
Two-way left turn.
Minimum speed limit.
No parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must and must not do. When you see this sign, you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before getting behind the wheel:

options.text: Are always aware of the risks they are taking.
Do not have good control over their body, mind, or vehicle.
Are better drivers because they are more careful than sober drivers.
Have quicker reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not have good control over their body, mind, or vehicle.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: If a vehicle using high beams comes toward you, you should look toward ____ of the road.

options.text: Either side
The center
The right side
The left side

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car is using high beams and will not dim them, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and helps you stay in your lane until the car passes.

questions.question: You need to use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian using a white cane because:

options.text: He or she is deaf.
He or she is a police officer.
He or she is blind.
He or she has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: He or she is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane means a person is blind. When you see a blind pedestrian with a cane or guide dog, slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances when they use a siren or horn and flashing lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so wait until the way is clear before moving.

questions.question: When approaching a traffic signal displaying a steady yellow arrow, drivers:

options.text: Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.
May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Have the right-of-way and may expect oncoming traffic to stop for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow will appear next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Cars in right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Watch for drunk drivers.
Dangerous curve ahead.
Bump in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black text on yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you to drive carefully when the road is wet because it may be slippery and harder to control your vehicle.
